title: The render storm
context: A developer asked an AI assistant to display sorted, filtered results in a table that re-renders on every keystroke of a search box. The suggested code works fine with a small dataset, but the input starts lagging noticeably once the table holds a few thousand rows.
question: Why does typing in the search box start lagging as the dataset grows?
options: filter and sort re-run on every render, including renders triggered by unrelated state changes, recomputing the full sort from scratch each time.
React re-mounts every Row component on each render because key is set to item.id.
localeCompare is asynchronous and blocks the main thread until it resolves.
toLowerCase() mutates the original item.name string, causing repeated re-renders.

explanation.theBug: filtered is recomputed inline in the component body, so it re-runs the filter and sort on every single render — not just when items or searchTerm actually change, but on any re-render this component participates in, including ones caused by parent updates unrelated to the table. For a few thousand rows, re-sorting on every keystroke, and every unrelated re-render, is expensive enough to visibly lag the input.
explanation.whyAIGeneratesThis: Filtering and sorting inline reads as simple, direct, and easy to follow, and it's functionally correct for any dataset size. Performance only becomes visible at scale, and knowing when a computation is expensive enough to warrant memoization requires reasoning about actual data size and render frequency, which isn't apparent from the code's structure alone.

theFix.commentary: Wrap the filter/sort pipeline in useMemo keyed on the inputs that actually affect its result, so it only recomputes when items or searchTerm change.

explanation.reviewHeuristic: Any non-trivial filter, sort, or transform computed directly in a component body is a useMemo candidate once the dataset can grow — check what re-renders trigger it before assuming it's cheap.
